---
title: "Module 1: Low-Dimensional Dynamics"
subtitle: "Part I of the syllabus, Sessions 1 to 9"
format: html
---

This module covers models with one or two state variables described by ordinary differential equations. You start with a single equation for an insect population and learn to find equilibria, decide their stability and follow them as parameters change. You then apply the same tools to epidemics, fit a model to data, and move to the plane, where oscillations, limit cycles, Hopf bifurcations and excitable systems appear [@strogatz2024nonlinear]. Lectures and laboratories alternate: each lecture is followed by a session in which you implement the model in Python. Reusable code is in `amlab/odes_1d/`, `amlab/odes_2d/` and `amlab/epidemics/`.

# Learning Goals

- Formulate a model as an ODE, and remove units to reduce the number of parameters.
- Find equilibria and decide their stability from the linearization.
- Recognize saddle-node and Hopf bifurcations, bistability and hysteresis.
- Integrate ODEs with `scipy.integrate.solve_ivp`, and validate the result against known solutions.
- Build interactive tools (Streamlit apps, Matplotlib animations and clickable parameter maps).
- Use SIR and SIS models to compute reproduction numbers, herd immunity thresholds and final sizes.
- Fit a model to incidence data and explain why the peak of an epidemic is hard to predict.
- Read a phase plane: nullclines, fixed points, limit cycles, excitability and relaxation oscillations.
